jobs.title: Geospatial Analyst
jobs.description:
Grounded in safety, quality, and ethics, our experts lead their fields with dedication, a creative spirit, and a vision for growth. We draw from more than 20 technical specialties worldwide and are devoted to fostering a community of diverse talents, backgrounds, and expertise. Here, you can apply your passion and collaborate with top environmental professionals on work that’s vital to our clients and the communities they serve.


Join a team that’s naturally committed to the environment.


We are seeking a talented Geospatial Analyst to join our team. You will be part of a collaborative group of GIS Specialists and Data Services professionals who deliver innovative solutions to both internal and external clients within an ESRI environment.


As a member of our Environmental Services Geospatial team—comprising over 160 geospatial professionals, you will help identify client needs and recommend optimal geospatial technologies and solutions to meet business objectives. Our team is solid and experienced, with diverse professional expertise ranging from 3 years to 29 years. We’re proud to say that our department has a strong retention rate, with employees staying with the company for more than 10 years on average.


As a Geospatial Analyst with Stantec you will provide technical support which includes mapping applications, spatial analysis, and map production; as well as mentoring and project support for assigned projects. This is a full\-time position working with our US West Environmental Services (ES) groups.


Your Key Responsibilities


* Compile, create and maintain spatial and non\-spatial information for a variety of platforms primarily involving ESRI ArcGIS Software (ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online (AGO)).
* Work in Windows 11 Enterprise and using MS Office suite of applications (Teams, Outlook, Word, Access, Excel, SharePoint).
* Produce custom thematic map products and carry out data analysis/summaries to support multidisciplinary project deliverables.
* Prepare web maps, online dashboards, and manage data for field survey crews, using applications and platforms which include Survey 123, Field Maps, and ArcGIS Online.
* Support geospatial field data collection efforts. Typical collected features include wetlands, waterways, sensitive species occurrences or habitats, cultural resources, paleontological resources, and geotechnical explorations.
* Adhere to established cartographic standards and Quality Assurance / Quality Control processes.
* Manage a wide variety of project\-specific and reference geospatial data in accordance with defined data management standards.
* Recognize when technical problems are developing and initiate appropriate corrective actions.
* Collaborate with existing GIS staff members working in other Stantec offices.
* Report to the US West Geospatial Team Lead.

Your Capabilities and Credentials


* Educated knowledge and experience working with Esri ArcGIS software suite, primarily ArcPro and ArcGIS Online, as well as ArcGIS Experience Builder, ArcGIS Field Maps, ArcGIS Survey123\.
* Experience building and using a GIS to solve problems, present results, and graphically report analytical data for multi\-disciplinary teams.
* Technical training and experience in GIS mapping, geospatial analysis, and geographic principles (e.g., map projections and coordinate systems).
* Demonstrate a knowledge of cartography and at least some understanding of graphic design.
* Ability to thrive in a fast\-paced, collaborative environment.
* Ability to meet project deadlines and understand how assigned tasks relate to project goals.
* Ability to maintain and establish effective working relationships.
* Ability to perform work accurately in a detail\-oriented environment.
* Exceptional visual, written, and verbal communication skills, problem\-solving abilities, and attention to detail.
* Understand how to convert data from older sources such as maps and books into accurate digital formats.
* Valid state driver’s license

Preferred


* Knowledge of Arcade, Python, and other GIS Programming languages.
* Working knowledge of CAD software, such as AutoCAD or MicroStation platforms.
* Experience performing environmental fieldwork using a GPS and post\-processing data is beneficial but not required.
* Experience working with LiDAR data.

Education and Experience


* Bachelors’ degree or equivalent in GIS, Geography, Geology, Environmental Science, or related field with demonstrated GIS training or coursework.
* 2\-3 years of experience providing professional (non\-coursework) related GIS Services is required
* Prior experience in the delivery of GIS products and analytical solutions as they relate to Utilities, Environmental Assessments, site assessments, CEQA, and the Environmental Regulatory Process is an asset.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee and other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.


About Stantec


Stantec is a global leader in sustainable engineering, architecture, and environmental consulting. The diverse perspectives of our partners and interested parties drive us to think beyond what’s previously been done on critical issues like climate change, digital transformation, and future\-proofing our cities and infrastructure. We innovate at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships to advance communities everywhere, so that together we can redefine what’s possible. \#StayInquisitive

### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you looking to be a part of a dynamic team of conservation\-minded scientists working to protect fish and wildlife resources in the coniferous forests of the Sierra Nevada (covering counties: Plumas, Butte, Sierra, Yuba, Nevada, Placer, El Dorado, Alpine, Amador and Calaveras), or the Coastal Mountain Range in Lake County?


The Department of Fish and Wildlife's Timberland Conservation and Fire Resiliency Program is seeking a motivated professional to work as an Environmental Scientist reviewing and evaluating Timber Harvest Plans,Timber Emergencies and Exemptions, and Vegetation Management Plans. This position also works in close collaboration with other Environmental Scientists and Senior Environmental Scientists, and with other state agencies as part of an interdisciplinary review team and may act as the staff lead and may provide consultative advice when working with applicants, local, state and federal agencies, stakeholders, and the general public.


Under the close supervision of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), and as a member of the California Department of Fish and Wildlife’s (Department) North Central Region (Region 2\) Timberland Conservation and Fire Resiliency Program, the incumbent is responsible for conducting identified activities related to the Forest Practice Rules, the Department’s Lake and Streambed Alteration Program (LSA), the California Endangered Species Act (CESA), the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and other laws, regulations, and Department policies, guidelines, and procedures pertaining to the protection of biological resources. The incumbent represents the Region and may act as the staff lead and provide consultative advice when working with applicants, local, state, and federal agencies, stakeholders, and the general public. Public contacts made in the course of this work are sensitive and involve a wide variety of special interest groups.


**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.


Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program: Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.


This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in\-person at least four (4\) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N\-22\-25\. Additional in\-office days may be required based on operational needs.


Link to Environmental Scientist Exam: CalCareers


**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.** During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.


You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position is eligible for partial telework (1\-day per week) based upon program need and will be headquartered from the Rancho Cordova regional office located at 1701 Nimbus Road, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670\. Based on institutional need, this position may be located in alternate locations and will be provided flexible hoteling space at any of the North Central Region's offices. This position requires the use of a computer for several hours each day, the completion of office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking to other locations; attendance at meetings and participation in conference calls. The position may require occasional travel throughout the State for site visits (30% of work time) including overnight travel, early mornings, and late nights. Must be able to work unusual and/or long hours; travel frequently; spend multiple days in the field assessing habitat conditions in inclement weather; walk in and through rough terrain; hike over uneven, steep, wet, and rough terrain with no vehicle access; operate a four\-wheel drive (4WD) vehicle off highway and over rough terrain; operate an all\-terrain vehicle (ATV); operate office equipment (computers, copies/scanners, telephones, iPads, global positioning system \[GPS] units, etc.); must possess a valid driver's license and be prepared to travel using a state vehicle with short notice for extended periods. The position requires the use of personal protective equipment, including, but not limited to, protective footwear, hardhat, gloves, helmet, and eye protection. Wearing a Department of Fish and Wildlife uniform is required as a condition of employment while conducting field work and public work duties on occasion.

**Summary**
-----------


You will serve as a Supervisory Interdisciplinary (General Engineer/Physical Scientist/Mathematician) with Bureau of Reclamation. You can make a difference in the West by assisting in meeting increasing water demands while protecting the environment.


**Duty Location: Sacramento, CA**


Engineers are on a Special Rate Table: $133,359 \- $160,638  

All other series fall under the Sacramento Pay Table: $117,984 \- $153,382


Learn more about this agency


  
**This job is open to**
-----------------------


### **The public**


U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.
### **Clarification from the agency**


This announcement is open to U.S. Citizen or National; and Career transition eligibles (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL).


  
**Duties**
----------


Some of the major duties you will perform include but are not limited to the following:

* Leads development, calibration, validation, and application of water resources models including CALSIM 3, DSM2, SCHISM, HEC\-RAS, water temperature, hydrology, and water quality models for CVP and Delta operations.
* Provides technical authority and policy guidance on systemwide water modeling issues to senior leadership and interagency partners.
* Designs and reviews complex studies incorporating hydrology, water supply, water quality, temperature, climate change, environmental standards, and compliance requirements.
* Oversees the entire modeling program including system operations, hydrologic, groundwater/surface water, temperature, power, and fisheries modeling systems.
* Establishes, maintains, and enforces modeling standards, technical adequacy requirements, QA/QC processes, and complete documentation practices.
* Identifies modeling capability gaps, evaluates modeling systems used by external partners, and ensures alignment and integration across programs.


\- Applies statistical analysis, optimization, scenario evaluation, and decision\-support methodologies to generate defensible analytical outputs.\- Translates complex scientific modeling results into executive\-ready materials, policy recommendations, and operational decision information.  

* Supervises engineers, scientists, and technical specialists through performance management, workload planning, training, hiring actions, discipline, and staff development.
* Ensures equitable access to training, recognition, promotion, and development opportunities through active implementation of EEO and inclusive leadership principles.
* Resolves workplace issues, grievances, and process barriers to improve organizational efficiency and mission delivery.
* Represents BOR in technical negotiations with Federal, State, local, tribal, NGO, and contractor partners on sensitive water operations and modeling issues.
* Develops technical specifications and contract requirements for model development or enhancement and oversees contractor performance.
* Monitors scientific literature, incorporates emerging modeling techniques, and ensures application of state\-of\-the\-science methodologies.
* Represents BOR in public meetings, interagency forums, regulatory settings, and litigation support requiring defense of modeling assumptions and results.

  
**Requirements**
----------------

* Must be a U.S. Citizen or National.
* Appointment subject to background investigation and favorable adjudication.
* Males born after 12\-31\-59 must be registered for Selective Service.
* Direct Deposit participation required.
* Successfully pass the E\-Verify employment verification check. To learn more, visit www.dhs.gov/EVerify/.
* Must have and maintain a valid driver's license throughout employment.
* A financial disclosure report will be required within 30 days of appointment.

As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1\-year probationary period during which your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest will be evaluated.  

  

This probationary period is an extension of the appointment process and therefore requires the agency to determine if continued employment would advance the public interest, meet the organization goals and mission of the agency, and/or otherwise promote the efficiency of the service. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, the agency will consider:
* your performance and conduct;
* the needs and interests of the agency;
* whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
* whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.

Under applicable law, the employment of an individual serving a probationary or trial period automatically terminates when that period ends unless the agency affirmatively certifies, in writing, that the individual's employment should continue and that their appointment should be finalized. In the absence of agency action to affirmatively certify continued employment beyond the probationary or trial period, such appointments are terminated.  

  

Upon completion of your probationary period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.  

  

This is a supervisory position that may require completion of a supervisory probationary period.

 **Job Description**


Without good understanding of ground conditions at project sites, delivering new projects or maintaining existing assets safely and efficiently can be challenging. That is why we offer multiple services including geotechnical site investigations, geologic and geo\-hazard evaluations, and geo\-consulting services focused on collecting and analyzing geo\-data.


Our Southern California group is looking to add a California\-licensed Senior Geologist to be a self\-starter who can lead effectively, be responsible for completing all facets of medium\-size site investigation and geology/geo\-hazard evaluations in accordance with California regulations and work toward managing large and complex projects. Senior professionals are registered geotechnical engineers or geologists, typically with advanced professional certiﬁcations, who manage and lead teams in execution of projects and pursuits. Through their leadership and use of technical and commercial know\-how, independent assessment and responsible judgment, they successfully deliver value to our clients. They may supervise more junior staff.

**Base Salary range for this job opportunity is $120,000 to $150,000 per year.**

**Job Responsibilities**

* Lead by example and place Quality, Health \& Safety, Security, and the protection of the Environment as core values while never intentionally placing employees, our processes, customers, or the communities in which we live and work at risk.
* Manage, direct and execute medium size projects from technical and commercial perspectives.
* Design, implement, and supervise field exploration programs, and detailed site characterization studies.
* Write technical reports and demonstrate proficient writing and verbal communication skills.
* Provide technical review of reports and proposals.
* Assign duties to the project team, answer questions, monitor progress, and check/ensure accuracy of completed work.
* Ensure that commitments to clients are met with respect to quality, timeliness, and budget.
* Support company’s pursuits of major projects.
* Make presentations to clients and staff.
* Support and encourage continuous improvement of the company’s processes.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

* Authorized to work in the United States, without restrictions.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or geology from accredited college or university required; master’s degree in engineering or geology from an accredited college or university highly preferred.
* California Professional Geologist (PG) License required, Certified Engineering Geologist (C.E.G.) License preferred.
* Have 7 years or more of geology, field investigation and project management experience required.
* Strong understanding and knowledge of geotechnical engineering, geology, engineering geology, geotechnical engineering and related disciplines, and must possess an overall understanding of typical project technical requirements and ﬁeld data acquisition procedures.

Job Title: Geologist III  

Location: Pleasanton, CA **Description/Job Summary** **POSITION DESCRIPTION**  

Join HGL’s growing team in California as a **Geologist III**. The Geologist III will provide environmental investigation, remediation, and deputy project management support services to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and other federal and state government clients throughout the western United States. This is a hybrid position based out of HGL’s Pleasanton, CA office, with 3 days a week in the office.  

As a Geologist III, you will work with our high performing HGL Teams and be responsible for supporting HGL’s portfolio of environmental investigation, remediation, and oversight projects for various agencies across the United States and territories. Initial duties will include providing remedial investigation oversight as well as oversight of remedial action (RA) projects. This position will also serve as a deputy project manager for large federal projects. Projects may include in situ thermal treatment, vapor intrusion, groundwater treatment (both in\-situ and pump\-and\-treat), mine\-waste cleanup, landfill cap construction, contaminated sediment removals, surface water treatment development and operations for organic and inorganics, and stabilization projects. **Responsibilities/Duties** **WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING**  

* Developing and providing technical review of planning documents and deliverables for environmental investigation and remediation projects.
* Interfacing with program and project managers, senior technical staff, the government customer, and RA Contractors.
* Developing technical skills for long\-term growth and development.
* Managing characterization and remediation projects for Federal clients.
* Overseeing and assisting with preparation of project deliverables including remediation work plans UFP\-QAPPs, FSPs, RI/FS Reports, SSHP/HASPs, and technical memoranda.
* Performing / conducting field subcontractor oversight inclusive of drilling, monitoring well construction, waste transportation and disposal, and heavy equipment operation.
* Assisting with data entry, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical and visualization tools.
* Utilizing approved digital and AI\-assisted tools, where appropriate, to support technical documentation, data analysis, project communications, and workflow efficiency.
* Providing technical support during investigation, planning, and execution phases.

**Minimum Requirements** **WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL**  

* Minimum of 6 years’ experience in the environmental field.
* Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Geophysics, Geological/Geotechnical Engineering or related field.
* PG or ability to obtain PG within one year.
* Strong writing and document review skills with prior experience contributing to the preparation of technical reports, memoranda, and work plans.
* Coordination of field subcontractors for environmental investigation and/or remediation activities. Knowledge and experience of CERCLA and EPA.

* Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

* Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

**GIS Analyst**

**Primary Function(s)** 

SYNCADD is actively recruiting a GIS Analyst to support a GIS and Real Property reconciliation effort at Joint Base Lewis\-McChord (JBLM), in Washington State. The GIS analyst will work on\-site at JBLM in a team environment supporting the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) to maintain and/or develop specific GIS data layers, maps and reports to address Army Real Property compliance requirements.

Candidates must have knowledge of geospatial principles, practices, and standards as well as experience with Microsoft office software; familiarity with creating and maintaining GIS features that comply with the Spatial Data Standards for Facilities, Infrastructure, and Environment (SDSFIE); and possess exceptional planning, critical thinking, analytical, and effective communication skills. Responsibilities include collecting, updating, and maintain GIS data in accordance with DPW and Army standards; performing data quality control and editing to meet SDSFIE 4\.0 GIS data standards; performing analysis and updates to existing and new GIS data to ensure Real Property compliance; filed data collection through GPS, field sensors, and field work or other means; map\-mapping and cartographic production; GIS analysis and modeling; and reporting.

**Responsibilities and Duties (but not limited to):** 

* Collaborating with team members and managers
* Managing multiple efforts and data requests concurrently
* Performing Real Property GIS data development and maintenance support
* Conducting data quality control checks, reporting, and standardization to SDSFIE
* Ensuring attribute and metadata development meet Army and JBLM standards
* Fulfilling requests for organizational geospatial data requests
* Performing enterprise GIS data maintenance
* Conducting Real Property and GIS data reconciliation
* Performing field data collection

**Required Qualifications:** 

* Bachelors or master’s degree in Geography, GIS. or related field
* 1\-4 years of experience with ArcGIS
* 1\-4 years of experience with the principles, practices, and methods related to GIS
* 1\-4 years of experience with Microsoft Office
* Due to federal contract requirements, US Citizenship is required for this position and must be able to obtain Security Clearances as needed

**Desired Qualifications:** 

* Experience with GPS (Trimble) data collection for GIS

jobs.title: Resource Geologist/Senior Resource Geologist
jobs.description:
We are SLR Consulting (Americas), a 1500\+ team of advisory, environmental, engineering, and regulatory professionals across Canada, the United States, and LATAM. We deliver environmental and sustainability services to our clients through the integration of over 30 advisory, technical environmental, and engineering disciplines to help clients address some of their most complex challenges around sustainability. We are Making Sustainability Happen.  



  

As our new **Resource Geologist/Senior Resource Geologist** , you will play an important role on a team whose work is essential to achieving this goal. Our projects encompass a wide spectrum, including geological modeling and resource estimation and reporting for various metals and depositional environments.  



  

**Responsibilities**  

* Perform geological modeling and mineralization domaining in Leapfrog software for diverse metals and depositional environments.
* Complete mineral resource estimates in Leapfrog Edge or other industry standard software for multiple commodities.
* Conduct geological database quality control analysis.
* Perform statistical evaluation of geological data.
* Collaborate with mining engineers, metallurgists, and other disciplines.
* Prepare project estimates, schedules, and reports.
* Provide client support and presentations.
* Contribute to business development efforts to expand our mining sector.
**Working @ SLR**  

With us, there is no doubt you’ll grow your subject\-matter expertise and industry knowledge. We care about investing in our employees for the long\-run, and if you ask our team, they’ll tell you that’s just one of the many benefits of working here. We want to be a place where you can experience career growth and satisfaction for many years.


**Here’s what else you’ll enjoy as part of our team:**  

* Competitive total compensation package including medical, dental, orthodontia, vision, FSA/HSA, generous PTO accrual, 10 paid holidays, 401(k) retirement account with company matching program, company paid life insurance, short \& long term disability insurance, and employee assistance program.
* The salary range for this position is $100,000 \- $120,000\. Final agreed upon. compensation will be commensurate with individual education, professional designation, experience, internal parity, and location.
* Full\-time, permanent role with opportunities for professional growth and advancement.
**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Geology or Geoscience. Masters Degree will be advantageous.
* Minimum 5 years of industry experience in minerals exploration, operations, or resource estimation.
* Significant experience in geomodelling and domaining in Leapfrog software is required.
* Practical experience in geostatistics and estimation methods in Leapfrog Edge preferred.
* Experienced in modelling various commodities in a variety of geological terranes, such as Carlin, porphyry, orogenic and skarn.
* Multi\-commodity experience in precious metals and base metals, with gold experience essential.
* Proficiency in Leapfrog software required, familiarity with other mine software such as Vulcan, MinePlan, Datamine, or MicroMine advantageous.

Join HGL’s growing team in California as a **Geologist III**. * Project Management Professional Certification (PMP).
